page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively. Similarly, single-threaded gzip compression is poor. However, multi-core execution scales to average levels, as demonstrated by average ratings in Geekbench multi-core, stress-ng multi-core, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks consistently register average performance, though the Passmark memory score is classified as weak.

Given its high memory density and average multi-core performance, the ecs.se1.4xlarge is suited for memory-intensive workloads that do not demand extreme single-thread processing power. Appropriate use cases include database operations, Redis caching, static web serving, and moderate software compilation tasks. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, and the baseline network speed of 3 Gbps may limit data-transfer-heavy operations. The instance offers a balanced qualitative cost efficiency for memory-heavy applications that can leverage parallel execution rather than raw single-core speed.
